prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 2024年重点信息化项目执行情况汇总表 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "项目" · longest unbreakable word 22px · one-line width 215px
  col 2: header "负责人" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 46px
  col 3: header "预算（万元）" · longest unbreakable word 60px · one-line width 92px
  col 4: header "进度" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 373px
  col 5: header "风险说明" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 1830px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
An earlier design attempt for this table was rejected by independent reviewers. Their comments: another layout was rated poor: 风险说明被压成约5字/行的窄条，行高被拉得很长；项目、负责人、进度也频繁断行。预算列虽勉强保住金额完整，整体仍难横向比较。 | another layout was rated poor: 预算列比A更窄，表头“预算（万元）”和金额被挤压；风险列仍只有约5—6字/行，项目名与进度竖排感强，阅读节奏碎。 | another layout was rated bad: 把更多宽度给了风险列，但项目/负责人只剩约2字/行，表头竖排，整表异常高；预算列也不足以稳放金额，拆东墙补西墙，最难扫读。 | another layout was rated acceptable: 唯一明显把长文本风险列作为主列，风险说明约9字/行，行高明显下降；但矫正过度，项目列窄到近乎逐字竖排，负责人、进度、预算也被压扁，表头和金额缺少呼吸。 | your previous preferred design was rated poor: 风险列约5字/行，项目与进度大量断行；列宽分配接近A/B但预算更窄，金额和表头受挤压，整体仍像几条竖条并排。 | another layout was rated poor: 风险列略宽于A/E，但仍只有约5字/行；各列平均偏窄，项目名、进度和预算都碎，缺少主次。
another layout was rated poor: 风险说明 is squeezed into a very narrow strip, making the table extremely tall; project and progress cells also fragment into short stacks that are hard to scan. | another layout was rated good: Best overall balance: project names and budget values remain comparatively readable, while the risk column gets enough width for continuous prose; some wrapping remains but row rhythm holds. | another layout was rated acceptable: Risk prose gets more room, but project, owner and budget columns are over-compressed, with names and numbers breaking awkwardly; a less balanced tradeoff. | your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: Project, owner and budget are reasonably legible, but the risk column is too narrow for its long text, creating tall dense rows. | another layout was rated acceptable: Similar to D but with an even tighter risk column; several short fields wrap awkwardly, making comparison harder. | another layout was rated poor: Risk gets the most space and the table is shortest, but project and owner columns collapse to one character per line, destroying the row identifiers.
